reviewBoundary: Sixteen independent new Junior2 practices: eight five-question reading pieces, four eight-gap choice clozes and four eight-response grammar passages. Complete inputs and individual evidence, distractor, variant and bound checks are supplied. Frozen sources supply matching level/form only. Author-self-review and engineering checks do not claim independent teacher validation, learner calibration or publication.

units.title: 初二阅读：电脑演示里的文件版本

materials.title: Laptop Demo Version
materials.text:
Our computer club prepared a short demonstration for parents. Mia made a slide file on the school laptop and saved a copy on a memory stick. On Thursday, she corrected a wrong club meeting time in the laptop file. She forgot to replace the older copy on the stick.

On Friday afternoon, the club moved to a larger room and used a different computer. The memory stick was the easiest way to transfer the presentation. During the practice, Amir noticed that the meeting time on the screen was wrong. Mia was surprised because she remembered correcting it.

Instead of changing the slide again without checking, they compared the two files. The laptop copy had Thursday's correction, while the memory-stick copy did not. They transferred the newer file and renamed it with the date and the word “final”. Then they opened that exact file on the presentation computer and checked the time once more.

After the demonstration, Mia wrote a note for the next group. A file could be correct in one place and outdated in another. The note suggested checking the version on the computer that would actually be used, not only the version on the creator's laptop.

questions.prompt: Where did Mia first correct the meeting time?
options: In the file on the school laptop.
questions.explanation: B正确：改校用笔电文件；D非纸信；A U盘没更新；C Amir手机未用。

questions.prompt: Why was the memory stick used on Friday?
options: The school had lost every laptop.
The demonstration used another computer in a larger room.
Mia wanted to keep the old time.
Parents were asked to bring memory sticks.
questions.explanation: B正确：换大房用另一电脑需转文件；A没丢设备；C非保留错时；D无家长U盘要求。

questions.prompt: What did comparing the files show?
options: Only the laptop copy included Thursday’s correction.
The older copy was more accurate.
The laptop file had never been saved.
questions.explanation: A正确：笔电新、U盘旧；B两版不同；D已存；C旧版错。

questions.prompt: What did the club do after transferring the newer file?
options: Opened that file on the presentation computer and checked it.
Changed the meeting day without asking.
questions.explanation: B正确：在实际演示电脑打开核时；D非全删；A再次查；C未擅改日期。

questions.prompt: What was Mia’s advice to the next group?
options: Check the version on the computer actually used for the event.
Use an old file whenever it is easier to find.
Assume every copy is updated at the same time.
Never save more than one presentation.
questions.explanation: A正确：实际使用端查版本；C正是误会；B旧版易找不代表对；D无禁备份。

units.title: 初二阅读：杯子押金与一张小票

materials.title: Cup Deposit Receipt
materials.text:
A new drink stall opened at the town's weekend fair. Customers could borrow a reusable cup by paying a small deposit in addition to the drink price. The stall would return the deposit when the customer brought back the cup and the matching token.

Ethan read only the large price board. He thought the whole amount was the cost of the drink, so he complained that it was expensive. The stall worker showed him the smaller notice explaining the deposit. Ethan put the token in his wallet rather than leaving it on the table.

Later, his friend Jo found an empty cup near a bench. She wanted to return it, but she had no token. The worker thanked her for bringing it back and explained that the token was needed for the deposit refund. This prevented one person's payment from being claimed more than once. Jo understood and did not take the cup home.

Before leaving the fair, Ethan returned his own cup with his token. He received the deposit back and compared the amount he had finally paid with the original price board. Next time, he said, he would read the details before deciding what a price included.

questions.prompt: What was needed for a deposit refund?
options: The borrowed cup and its matching token.
Only a photograph of the stall.
The name of a friend at the fair.
questions.explanation: B正确：杯与对应token；C照片、A瓶、D朋友姓名均非退款条件。

questions.prompt: Why did Ethan first think the drink was expensive?
options: He had bought drinks for every customer.
The worker had refused to show him the price.
He had already lost his wallet.
He thought the deposit was part of the drink’s final cost.
questions.explanation: D正确：只看大牌把押金算最终价；B价格公开；A非给所有人买；C钱包还在。

options: Claimed Ethan’s deposit with his token.
Returned a found cup without a token.
questions.explanation: C正确：捡空杯无token归还；A未拿Ethan凭证；D不带回；B已归还。

questions.prompt: Why did the stall require the token?
options: To make customers buy a second drink.
To identify which bench a cup had been on.
To avoid refunding one payment more than once.
To stop anyone returning a lost cup.
questions.explanation: C正确：防同押金多次领；A未强买；B非追踪长椅；D仍感谢归还只是退款需凭证。

questions.prompt: What did Ethan decide to do in future?
options: Always keep borrowed cups at home.
Pay the deposit twice to save time.
Read what a price includes before judging it.
questions.explanation: D正确：先读细则再判断价格；C反向；A、B均无此决定。

units.title: 初二阅读：皮影幕布的测试

materials.title: Shadow Screen Test
materials.text:
Our drama club made a short shadow play for younger pupils. We built a screen from a sheet and used a lamp behind it. In the art room, the figures looked clear, so we thought we were ready.

The performance room was much larger. At the first rehearsal there, people in the back row said that the figures were difficult to see. Some club members wanted a more powerful lamp, but our teacher asked us to test the position of the screen first. A wide window was allowing light to fall across its front.

We moved the screen away from the window and tried again with the same lamp. The shadows became clearer. Next, we checked whether the small paper tree in the final scene could be seen from the back. Its narrow branches disappeared, so we made a simpler tree with broader branches. We kept the old one in our project folder to show why it had changed.

On the day, two pupils sat briefly in the back row before the audience arrived. They checked the view while the actors tested the figures. We had learned that a successful rehearsal in one room was not enough to guarantee the same result somewhere else.

questions.prompt: What problem appeared in the larger room?
options: Back-row viewers could not see the figures clearly.
The actors had forgotten every line.
The paper tree was too heavy to carry.
questions.explanation: A正确：后排看不清；B未忘词；D幕在；C问题细枝不可见非重量。

questions.prompt: What did the teacher suggest testing first?
questions.explanation: D正确：先测幕位置；A票价、B结局、C全城灯无据。

questions.prompt: What improved the shadows without changing the lamp?
options: Putting the lamp in the project folder.
Moving the screen away from the window.
Removing all figures from the play.
questions.explanation: B正确：避窗前光后影清楚；A非把灯藏文件；D仍演；C会增外光而非做法。

questions.prompt: Why was a simpler paper tree made?
options: Its broader branches would be easier to see from the back.
The audience needed a tree they could take home.
The original had the wrong name.
The teacher did not allow old work in the folder.
questions.explanation: A正确：原窄枝消失，换宽枝；C非名称；D旧件反留文件；B无分发。

questions.prompt: What did the club check before the audience arrived?
options: The price of a new window.
The view from the back row in the actual room.
Whether every pupil owned a lamp.
Whether the art room was empty.
questions.explanation: B正确：实际房后排测试视角；D美术室空非点；C自有灯、A窗价均无关。

units.title: 初二阅读：列车座位旁的便条

materials.title: Train Seat Note
materials.text:
When my aunt and I boarded the train, a small bag was on the seat beside our reserved places. I assumed someone was keeping the seat for a friend. My aunt pointed to a paper note attached to the handle: “Please ask the conductor before moving this bag.”

We did not open it or take it to another carriage. My aunt found the conductor, who said that a passenger had left it while helping an older relative off the train. The passenger had already called the station and would collect the bag when the train returned that evening. The conductor moved it to the staff cupboard.

Once the seat was clear, another passenger sat there. She thanked us, but my aunt explained that the conductor had dealt with it. On the journey, I asked why we had not simply placed the bag on a luggage shelf. My aunt said that a place which seemed obvious to us might not be the place where staff expected to find it.

I had first seen the bag as an obstacle between me and a comfortable seat. The note and the conductor's explanation made me notice the unfinished journey of its owner as well.

questions.prompt: What did the narrator first assume about the bag?
options: It was owned by the aunt.
It was reserving a seat for someone’s friend.
It had been placed there by the station café.
It contained a present for the conductor.
questions.explanation: B正确：起初以为占座等友；D礼物、A姨妈、C咖啡馆均非初猜。

questions.prompt: What did the attached note ask people to do?
options: Move it to any empty carriage.
Open the bag to read its contents.
Take it off at the next stop.
Ask the conductor before moving it.
questions.explanation: D正确：搬前问列车员；B开包、A任意车厢、C下站带下均未请求。

questions.prompt: Why had the owner left the bag?
options: The owner had given it to the aunt.
The owner had been helping an older relative off the train.
The owner wanted to stop anyone sitting down.
The conductor had refused to carry it.
questions.explanation: B正确：帮老亲属下车遗留；C并非占座动机；D未拒；A没送姨妈。

questions.prompt: Where did the conductor put the bag?
questions.explanation: B正确：移工作人员橱；A没随便上架；C、D无此安排。

questions.prompt: What changed in the narrator’s view?
options: The bag became connected with its owner’s interrupted journey.
The bag was seen as proof that the train was empty.
The narrator decided every bag should reserve a seat.
The narrator stopped believing any written note.
questions.explanation: A正确：从障碍看见主人未完行程；C非所有包占座；D信便条；B非空车证据。

units.title: 初二阅读：迎新活动的任务徽章

materials.title: Orientation Badge Choice
materials.text:
At a weekend camp, new visitors could collect badges by completing small tasks. The organisers wanted the badges to help people explore the campsite, not to turn the afternoon into a race. Each task card explained what to do and where to ask for help.

I chose a card called “Find the Oldest Tree”. I expected to look for the tallest tree. The activity leader asked me to read the question again. A tall tree was not always the oldest, and the campsite's tree records were kept at the visitor desk. I went there and compared three planting dates.

The oldest recorded tree was beside the kitchen, although it was shorter than a large tree near the gate. I took the task card to the leader and explained how I had decided. She gave me a badge after hearing the reason, not simply after seeing a tree name written down.

My younger cousin completed only two tasks while I completed four. At the closing meeting, the organisers invited each person to share one thing they had discovered. Nobody announced a winner based on the number of badges. My cousin described a small insect house that I had walked past without noticing.

questions.prompt: What was the main purpose of the badge tasks?
options: To keep visitors beside the gate all day.
To help visitors explore the campsite.
To prevent anyone asking for help.
questions.explanation: C正确：徽章帮助探索非竞赛；A速度、B守门、D禁问均不合。

questions.prompt: What mistake did the narrator nearly make?
options: Choosing a task with a title.
Assuming the tallest tree must be the oldest.
questions.explanation: C正确：先以最高当最老；D/B是正确核查；A任务标题不是错误。

questions.prompt: How was the oldest recorded tree identified?
options: By choosing the tree nearest the gate.
questions.explanation: B正确：比三栽植日期；A徽章数、C声大、D门口高树均非凭据。

questions.prompt: What did the leader want before giving the badge?
options: Proof that the cousin had fewer badges.
questions.explanation: A正确：先听理由；C非所有树照片；B无比较徽章条件；D无不再来要求。

questions.prompt: What did the final meeting show?
options: Everyone had noticed the same insect house.
People could discover different things without a badge-count winner.
The cousin had discovered nothing useful.
questions.explanation: C正确：分享发现无按数获胜，弟两任务也有作者漏见昆虫屋；B人人可分享；D有发现；A作者未注意。

units.title: 初二阅读：食堂意见卡的两种问题

materials.title: Canteen Comment Cards
materials.text:
The school canteen asked students to comment on a new lunch menu. At first, the card had one question: “Did you like today's lunch?” The cook received many yes-or-no answers but little information about what to change.

Our student council helped write a new card. It asked students to name the dish they had eaten, say one thing that worked well and suggest one specific improvement. The cook explained that “bad” was hard to act on, while “the vegetables were cold when I reached the table” described a problem that could be checked.

We also left a box for students who had not eaten the new meal. They could explain why, such as bringing food from home or arriving after a dish had run out. Their comments were kept separate from opinions about taste, because they described a different experience.

After a week, the cook showed us two changes. Staff had adjusted the order of serving hot dishes, and the menu board now showed when a popular choice was no longer available. The cook did not claim that everyone would enjoy every meal. The aim was to understand which practical changes could help, using comments that described what had actually happened.

questions.prompt: What was limited about the original comment card?
options: It was only for visitors from other schools.
It mostly produced yes-or-no answers without useful detail.
It contained every student’s favourite recipe.
It asked students to write a complete novel.
questions.explanation: B正确：单问喜否少可改细节；D不写小说；A本校学生；C非配方全表。

questions.prompt: Why was the cold-vegetable comment useful?
options: It removed the need to name a dish.
It proved nobody liked any vegetable.
It described a particular problem staff could check.
It was shorter than the word “bad”.
questions.explanation: C正确：冷到桌边是可核问题；B不证全不爱；A仍要求菜名；D句显更长。

questions.prompt: Why were comments from non-eaters kept separately?
options: Those students were not allowed to have opinions.
They always wanted the same dish.
They concerned a different experience from tasting the meal.
questions.explanation: D正确：未吃经历与口味评价不同；B仍可留言；A非不知名；C无同菜断言。

questions.prompt: What did the menu board begin to show?
options: When a popular dish was no longer available.
questions.explanation: B正确：显示热门菜售完；A非全贴评价；C私址、D明年餐非改动。

questions.prompt: What was the aim of the changes?
options: To guarantee that every student would love every dish.
To remove all choices from the menu.
To use specific experiences to improve practical parts of the service.
questions.explanation: C正确：基于发生事件做可行改进；A明确不保证人人爱；B不撤选项；D还用意见。

units.title: 初二阅读：小动物照片里的参照物

materials.title: Small Creature Scale
materials.text:
Our nature club displayed photographs of insects found in the school garden. The large prints made tiny creatures look impressive, but younger visitors could not tell how big they really were. One child thought a beetle was the size of a shoe.

The teacher did not ask us to put a ruler beside every live insect. Instead, we checked the notes made when the pictures were taken. For some photographs, the photographer had recorded the approximate length. Others showed a familiar object, such as a leaf whose size we had measured. We added short captions only where we had a reasonable basis for the estimate.

One especially clear photograph had no size note and no useful object for comparison. We kept it in the display but wrote that its exact scale was unknown. The picture still showed details of the beetle's legs, even though it could not answer every question about the animal.

Before the display opened, we asked two pupils from another class to read the captions. They helped us replace the term “enlargement factor” with a simpler explanation. The aim was to make the photographs easier to understand, not to make uncertain measurements look exact.

questions.prompt: What misunderstanding did the large prints create?
options: The children could no longer recognise a garden.
Everyone believed the insects lived inside shoes.
Some visitors misjudged the insects’ actual size.
Visitors thought every photo had been lost.
questions.explanation: C正确：放大后误判实际体积，一儿童以为鞋大；D未丢；A仍是花园；B只尺寸比较非住鞋。

questions.prompt: What did the club use before adding size captions?
options: Only a guess based on the printed page.
A rule saying every beetle was identical.
Photographers’ notes or a measured comparison object.
questions.explanation: D正确：拍摄笔记或已测叶参照；A非纯猜；B不同甲虫不等；C价无关。

questions.prompt: What happened to the picture with no reliable size information?
options: It stayed on display with the scale uncertainty stated.
It was removed as completely useless.
It was given an invented exact measurement.
It was labelled as a photograph of a shoe.
questions.explanation: A正确：保留并说明未知比例；C未编；B还可看腿细节；D非鞋照。

questions.prompt: Why were outside pupils asked to read the captions?
options: To check whether the explanation was easy to understand.
To measure every insect in the garden again.
To write a new school timetable.
questions.explanation: A正确：他班读者帮改术语使易懂；D相机、B重测所有虫、C课表均未做。

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the display’s final approach?
options: A large print was always an exact life-size record.
Every photo had to answer every possible question.
Useful detail could be shown while uncertainty remained visible.
Only photographs without captions were allowed.
questions.explanation: C正确：细节有用但不装精确，未知写明；B一图不答所有；D加题注；A放大非原大。

units.title: 初二阅读：新同学听到的活动室名称

materials.title: New Student Room Name
materials.text:
When Daniel joined our school, I offered to show him where the lunchtime clubs met. I told him the games club was in “the old lab”. He thanked me, and I thought the directions were clear.

At lunch, I found him waiting outside a science classroom on the second floor. The games club was downstairs in a room that had been an old laboratory many years before. Most students used its nickname, but the door now said “Activity Room B”. Daniel had followed the meaning of my words, not the place I had intended.

I took him downstairs and apologised for the confusing instruction. Afterwards, we checked the club notice together. It also used “old lab” without giving the official room name or floor. We asked the club leader to change it to “Activity Room B, ground floor, beside the library stairs”.

A week later, another new pupil found the club without help. Daniel said the new wording had explained the place instead of testing whether someone already knew the school's history. I realised that familiar directions could leave out exactly the information a newcomer needed.

questions.prompt: Why did the narrator first think the directions were clear?
options: The nickname was familiar to existing students.
The games club was still a science lesson.
The official room name was written in the narrator’s message.
Daniel had drawn the room’s old plan.
questions.explanation: A正确：校内常用旧实验室昵称，作者默认懂；B不是科学课；D未画旧图；C初未给官方名。

questions.prompt: Where did Daniel wait at first?
questions.explanation: B正确：二层科学教室外；A真正方向；C没到社团；D非校门。

questions.prompt: What was the current official room name?
questions.explanation: B正确：门写Activity Room C；C/A/D不是门牌。

questions.prompt: What was added to the revised notice?
options: The official name, floor and a nearby landmark.
A warning that newcomers should not join.
questions.explanation: A正确：房名地层图书馆楼梯旁；C不只历史；B非老师名录；D欢迎新生非禁入。

options: Only a spoken invitation can explain any room.
School history is unnecessary in every lesson.
Directions must include information that insiders may take for granted.
New pupils should guess every nickname.
questions.explanation: C正确：熟人默认信息正是新生需要；D不要求猜；B非全盘否历史；A书面改后有效。

units.title: 初二完形：寄回来的明信片

materials.title: Postcard Returned Address
materials.text:
During a holiday, I bought a postcard of the town harbour for my cousin. I wrote a long message and copied her address from an old notebook. Two weeks after I returned home, the card arrived at ____1____ own house. A sticker said that the receiver had moved.

At first, I was annoyed with the post office. Then I phoned my cousin and ____2____ that she had sent her new address to our family months earlier. I had looked at the first notebook I could find instead of checking the recent message.

My cousin was not upset. She wanted to hear about the harbour and asked me to read the message ____3____ the phone. I described the fishing boats and the small café where I had written the card. The story made her laugh, even though the postcard had travelled in the ____4____ direction.

I put the card in a new envelope and wrote the correct address. This time, I asked my cousin to ____5____ each line before I posted it. I kept the old sticker in my notebook as a reminder to check information that might have changed.

A few days later, she sent a photo of the card on her desk. It had arrived late, ____6____ the message still meant something to her. I had thought of a postcard as a simple object moving from one place to another. Now I saw how much it depended ____7____ a small piece of accurate information. I updated the address in my notebook ____8____ I would not make the same mistake again.

questions.explanation: A正确：叙述我寄给表亲却退我自己家，my own；B她家即目的地非退回；D他们、C我们复数不合明确第一人称个人住处。
A正确：打电话发现新址早发；C忘记相反；B拒绝、D借入不接that获知事实。
A正确：over the phone电话中，D下方、C横穿、B在众人间非该媒介固定用法。
A正确：投递退回错误方向，非D安静、B昂贵、C著名方向。
A正确：寄前逐行核对地址；D藏、B撕、C涂色均违求正确。
A正确：虽晚但有意义转折，C除非、D直到、B因为不表达该反差。
D正确：depend on固定依赖；C for、A with、B by均不合该动词所需介词。
D正确：更新地址为不重错目的so that；B仿佛、A即使当、C只要都非目的连接。

units.title: 初二完形：棋钟前的第一盘棋

materials.title: Chess Clock Demonstration
materials.text:
I joined an after-school chess group because I liked solving problems, but I had never played with a chess clock. At my first meeting, I watched two experienced players press a button after each move. I thought the clock only showed ____1____ it was time to go home.

The group leader explained its purpose using a short practice game. Each player had a limited amount of thinking time. After making a move, a player pressed the button so the other person's time would ____2____. The clock was part of the game, not the room timetable.

During my first try, I was so busy choosing a move that I forgot the button. My partner did not use the mistake to ____3____ me. She pointed to the clock and let me practise the action again. We agreed that this game was for learning how the equipment worked.

I still lost, but I could explain ____4____ I had spent most of my time. One difficult choice had taken several minutes, while I had moved too quickly in a simpler position. The clock helped me notice a habit rather than simply telling me that I was ____5____.

At the next meeting, I asked for another practice game before joining the main activity. I did not expect to become an expert ____6____. I wanted one part of the process to feel less unfamiliar. This made it easier to concentrate on the board. By the end of the month, pressing the button was no longer a separate problem ____7____ every move. I had learned that a small routine could take practice, even when the main activity was something I already ____8____.

questions.explanation: A正确：showed whether是否该回家；C whose所属、D where地点、B which限定选物均不填该完整从句。
C正确：自己按后对方时间开始；A停止是自己钟；B消失、D睡非计时动作。
B正确：不借错使难堪而教重练，C欢迎、A加入、D感谢均非这种负面行为的否定对照。
B正确：where表示在哪个选择环节花时，后句困难选择数分钟；D/A人物，C后缺名词不成该宾从。
D正确：时间慢只是一面，D slow有逻辑；A沉默、B空、C圆不描述时钟可能反馈的棋手速度。
A正确：不指望立即专家；D外面、C昨天、B楼上非成长期望时间。
D正确：按键发生每步之后，after；A unless缺从句，C above与B beside为空间关系，不能表达该步后时间。
D正确：喜欢棋才加入，既有兴趣主活动也需小常规练习；C拥有、B关闭、A遗忘不合。

units.title: 初二完形：陶杯先去等待架

materials.title: Pottery Waiting Shelf
materials.text:
Our art class made small clay cups for a school display. I finished shaping mine before most of my classmates and wanted to paint it immediately. The teacher asked me to put it on a shelf and ____1____. The clay needed time to dry before the next stage.

I was disappointed because the cup looked complete. The teacher showed me another piece that had dried too quickly on one side. A crack had appeared near its base. The outside shape was only ____2____ of the work; the condition of the material mattered too.

We wrote our names on the boards beneath our cups, not on the shelf itself. This would help us find the right pieces even if the teacher had to ____3____ them. I added a small pencil sketch of my handle beside my name.

The following week, my cup was still on the board, but its handle had a tiny line where it joined the body. I decided to ask for advice first. I told the teacher ____4____ trying to cover it with paint. She checked it and explained what could be done at that stage.

Some cups could continue towards the display, while others would remain examples of what we had learned. My cup was one of the second group. I felt sad, but the teacher asked me to describe the problem and my next ____5____. On my next attempt, I paid more attention to how the parts joined.

At the display, I showed both cups with a short note. Visitors could see a difference, not just a perfect final object. The first cup had not become ____6____ simply because it could not be used as planned. It helped explain the ____7____ behind the second. I understood why a shelf for waiting could be as important ____8____ a table for making.

questions.explanation: A正确：等干再下一阶段；D跑、C卖、B喊不合干燥。
B正确：外形仅工作一部分，材料也要紧；D全部与后句相反；A无部分、C任一不合结构。
D正确：若老师挪杯，板上名仍辨识；A尝、C借、B穿不合。
D正确：前句ask for advice first明确先询后涂，before；C across、A among不表该先后；B after会反转明确的first顺序。
C正确：讨论下次尝试，后句next attempt；A到达、D假期、B口袋无关改进。
A正确：旧杯仍展示学习价值非无用；B著名、C吵、D拥挤不符合价值判断。
D正确：说明第二杯背后学习过程；A价格未定，B地址、C天气无关。
D正确：as important as同级比较；B/from、C/than、A/to不合。

units.title: 初二完形：有云的观星晚上

materials.title: Cloudy Star Evening
materials.text:
The astronomy club planned an evening in the school garden. I had never looked through a telescope before and expected to see the same colourful images that appeared in a book. The club leader asked us to bring warm clothes and plenty of ____1____.

Clouds covered the sky when we arrived. Instead of sending everyone home, the leader showed us how the telescope was set up. We learned not to ____2____ its position while another person was using it. Each small adjustment changed what could be seen.

After half an hour, a clear space opened between the clouds. The leader invited us to look one at a time. I saw a pale shape, much less colourful than the printed picture, and felt ____3____. I wondered whether I had done something wrong.

The leader explained that the book image had been made using a different process and much more time. It was not a simple ____4____ of what any person would see at a glance. Understanding this helped me pay attention to the shape that was actually there.

My friend noticed a detail I had missed and described where to look. When I tried again, I could find it too. The evening became a shared search ____5____ a chance to collect a perfect picture. We kept notes about the weather and what we had seen.

On the way home, I still liked the book's bright photographs. However, I no longer expected every direct view to ____6____ them. The small pale shape had been interesting once I knew what I was looking for. I wrote down one question for the next meeting, ____7____ the clouds might prevent us from using the telescope again. There would still be something to learn ____8____ waiting for the sky to clear.

questions.explanation: A正确：观星需耐心后面等云；D家具、B交通、C行李非bring plenty of该活动心理准备。
A正确：别人用时别改位置，每调会变目标；B描述、D记住、C画图不影响观察位。
A正确：看不如彩照而失望怀疑出错；C自豪相反；D饱、B迟不描述心理。
C正确：书中经处理长时间图不是任何人一眼所见的简单记录record；B票、A价、D理由不表达图像记录关系。
B正确：共享寻找取代收完美图，rather than；C因、D除、A根据不表达两种活动目标对比。
A正确：不再期待目视匹配书图；D修、B藏、C携带不合them指照片。
D正确：即使下次云挡仍准备问题，even if；C一就、A目的、B直到不成让步。
D正确：while waiting为等待时；B/A空间不合，C except waiting与有得学意义不合。

units.title: 初二语法：农场指示牌的英文说明

materials.title: Farm Sign Translation
materials.text:
Last month, our English club visited a small farm that was preparing to welcome visitors from other countries. The owner ____1____ (ASK) us to read some new English signs. She wanted ____2____ (KNOW) whether the directions were clear.

One sign pointed to a building ____3____ had once been a store room. It was now a place to wash hands. The picture on the sign showed a tap, but the written name still described the old use of the building.

We suggested a new name and wrote it ____4____ (CAREFUL) on a draft card. The owner checked the wording with a teacher before putting it up. She did not simply assume that a student suggestion had to be correct.

A second sign stood ____5____ the gate and the car park. We moved it closer to the path after asking the owner. Visitors approaching from the road could see it more ____6____ (EASY) there.

After ____7____ (FINISH) our notes, we walked the route again. Our guide asked us to imagine that we had never visited the farm before. It was a useful way to test ____8____ (WE) own explanations.

questions.explanation: Last month过去asked谓语。
want to do不定式。
building作had been主语，which/that；where不能作从句主语。
修饰wrote副词carefully。
between the gate and car park明确两者之间。
修饰see用more easily。
After介词后动名词。
own explanations前物主our。

units.title: 初二语法：渡轮旅行中的小册子

materials.title: Ferry Island Notebook
materials.text:
Our school group took a ferry to an island last Friday. Before we boarded, the teacher ____1____ (GIVE) each of us a small notebook. She asked us ____2____ (WRITE) down one question during the journey.

I sat beside a window ____3____ looked towards the harbour. There were many different boats, but I did not know what most of them were used for. A member of staff explained the purpose of one boat without leaving her work.

The crossing was ____4____ (SHORT) than I had expected. When we arrived, I still had several questions in my notebook. The teacher said that we did not have to answer all of ____5____ (THEY) immediately.

After ____6____ (WALK) to the visitor centre, we looked at an island map. It helped us decide which questions could be explored on our planned route. We listened ____7____ (QUIET) while a guide described the old harbour.

At the end of the day, we compared the questions with our first impressions. The notebook was not full of facts copied from signs. It also showed ____8____ we had wanted to understand before we knew very much about the place.

questions.explanation: 过去登船前发本，gave或had given均可。
ask somebody to do不定式。
window作looked主语which/that。
than比较shorter。
of后宾格them。
after介词后动名词walking。

questions.prompt: Gap 7 (QUIET): Use the adverb ending in -ly.  Write one word.
questions.explanation: 修饰listened用quietly，指定标准-ly副词避免平义变体歧义。
what作wanted to understand宾语，引导名词从句。

units.title: 初二语法：画室中两只相似的瓶子

materials.title: Painted Vase Description
materials.text:
Our art class borrowed two old vases from a teacher's collection. They looked similar, but one was much ____1____ (HEAVY) than the other. We were not allowed ____2____ (LIFT) them until the teacher had explained how to hold them.

I chose the blue vase for my drawing. It had a small mark near the bottom ____3____ was easy to miss. The teacher asked me whether I wanted to include that detail or draw only the general shape.

While I ____4____ (DRAW), my friend described the flowers on the other vase. We realised that looking at an object and explaining it in words were different skills. Neither was automatically ____5____ (EASY) than the other.

After ____6____ (COMPLETE) our first pictures, we exchanged seats and looked again. From my friend's position, the small mark on the blue vase was hidden. I understood why two accurate drawings could show different details.

Before the lesson ended, the teacher put both vases back in ____7____ (THEY) boxes. We kept our drawings beside the written descriptions, so we could compare ____8____ we had noticed from each place.

questions.explanation: than要求heavier。
be allowed to do不定式。
mark作was easy主语，which/that。
I单数过去叙事可过去进行或一般过去。
than比较easier。
after介词接completing。
boxes前their物主。
what作noticed宾语，引导compare宾从。

units.title: 初二语法：练习比分中的人数差异

materials.title: Practice Score Context
materials.text:
Our basketball club compared the scores from two practice afternoons. At first, one group seemed ____1____ (GOOD) than the other because it had scored more points. The coach asked us ____2____ (LOOK) at the notes beside the totals.

On the first afternoon, six players had taken part. On the second, there ____3____ (BE) only four. The games had also lasted for different lengths of time. A total could be correct without being a fair comparison of the same situation.

The player ____4____ had written the notes showed us the starting times. We checked them ____5____ (CAREFUL) instead of guessing from memory. Then we agreed to describe the scores with their conditions attached.

For the next session, the coach suggested ____6____ (USE) the same number of players and the same game length. He said this would make one comparison more useful, though it would not measure every part of ____7____ (WE) skill.

After the session, we understood the numbers better. We had not changed a score to make it look nicer. We had learned ____8____ a number needed an explanation before someone used it to judge a team.

questions.explanation: than比较good不规则better。
ask somebody to look不定式。
there were only four players复数过去。
player作从句主语who/that。
修饰checked用carefully。
suggest doing，using动名词。
skill前our。
learned that得知事实、why理解原因、how理解数字需解释的情形均可接该完整从句；which无选择范围及可充成分。
